tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded run logs show a successful workflow for navigating Magento Admin -> Catalog -> Attributes -> Manage Attributes; filling the filter row (Attribute Code and Attribute Label), selecting Scope, clicking Search, locating the attribute row for 'color', and clicking its Edit anchor. The session also demonstrated opening Add New Attribute and filling the New Attribute form, but save detection was inconclusive (no success message captured). Recorded element hashes provide deterministic interaction targets for inputs, selects and buttons.

Task Definition:
- Automate the exact routine: open Manage Attributes, apply filters (attribute_code, frontend_label, is_global), run Search, find the row matching attribute_code and open its Edit page. This tool does NOT perform authentication (session must already be authenticated) and does not perform conditional branching: it always attempts the same sequence using provided inputs.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate to Manage Attributes page using a direct URL constructed from {base_url}.
2) Confirm page loaded and controls present (diagnostic extraction).
3) Input the attribute_code and frontend_label into the filter row.
4) Set the Scope select to the provided is_global visible text or numeric value.
5) Click Search to refresh the grid.
6) Wait briefly for the grid to update (configurable wait_seconds_after_search).
7) Extract grid content to identify the row matching attribute_code and capture the edit anchor href (diagnostic extraction).
8) Click the first anchor in that row (typical Magento pattern where the label/code links to edit). Uses recorded elementHash for determinism and an XPath fallback: //tr[td[1][normalize-space() = '{attribute_code}']]//a[1].
9) Extract page content of the edit page to verify navigation and provide selectors for further automation.

Variable Identification (inputs required):
- base_url (required): needed to reliably navigate to the Manage Attributes page.
- attribute_code (required): used as the exact text match in the first grid column to find the row and its edit link.
- frontend_label (optional): secondary filter for the label column; pass empty string to skip.
- is_global (optional): visible scope option or numeric value (0/1/2). If empty string passed, the tool will not change the scope selection.
- wait_seconds_after_search (optional): brief wait to let server render the filtered grid.

Step Optimization:
- Replaced menu-click navigation with a single deterministic navigation step to the known Manage Attributes URL (faster and less fragile).
- Used recorded elementHash values for the Attribute Code input (b8d714807e), Attribute Label input (b09783d79a), Scope select (9b26bb1a98) and Search button (b48f68f305) to avoid brittle generic selectors. Where elementHash might not resolve, an XPath fallback is provided (//tr[td[1][normalize-space() = '{attribute_code}']]//a[1]) to locate the edit anchor.
- Eliminated optional exploratory steps. The tool follows a strict linear sequence to accomplish only the single task (filter & open edit) as requested.
- Included extraction steps before and after filter/search and after clicking Edit so the caller can validate success (presence of messages, attribute edit form elements, or href patterns). This helps detect save success if used to create attributes in a separate flow.

Limitations & Notes:
- The tool assumes the browser session is already authenticated in admin. Do NOT include login steps here because the automation environment should manage authentication separately.
- Some Magento admin pages require JavaScript for full functionality (AJAX grid refresh, clickable row anchors). If JS is disabled in the runner, selectors and clicks may not behave; ensure JS is enabled in the automation environment.
- XPath selectors are preferred for text matching (match first td text == {attribute_code}). Pure CSS text matching is unreliable in many drivers; CSS fallbacks are included only for environments that support :has/:contains or when a row index is acceptable.

Result:
- The tool is deterministic, parameterized, and uses recorded stable element hashes with XPath fallbacks. It performs exactly one task: locate an attribute by code (filter) and open its Edit page. Use this tool as a building block for create/edit flows; a separate tool can perform attribute creation to keep single-purpose semantics.
name: magento_admin_attribute_open_edit
description: Automates navigating to Magento admin Manage Attributes, applying column filters (attribute code, frontend label, scope), running Search, locating the attribute row by attribute code and clicking its Edit anchor to open the attribute edit page. Assumes the session is already authenticated in the browser context. Uses recorded stable element hashes and XPath fallbacks where available.

steps.description: Open the Manage Attributes page directly (deterministic navigation to the grid).
Extract page structure and messages to ensure we're on the expected page before interacting.
steps.goal: Confirm Manage Attributes page and that filter controls and grid are present (used for diagnostics).

steps.description: Fill the Attribute Code filter input with the exact attribute code ({attribute_code}). Uses recorded elementHash for deterministic targeting.
Fill the Attribute Label filter input with the provided frontend label ({frontend_label}). Leave empty string to skip.
Select the Scope filter. Provide visible text (e.g., 'Global') or numeric mapping (e.g., '2'). If empty string is supplied the step will select no option (keeps default).
Click the Search / Apply Filters button to refresh the grid with the entered filters.
Wait a short period for the grid to refresh. Controlled by input {wait_seconds_after_search} if caller overrides it.
Extract the grid rows and specifically search for a row whose first cell equals {attribute_code}. Capture the row index and any visible anchor hrefs for diagnostics.
steps.goal: Locate the attribute row for {attribute_code} and capture any edit anchor href if present.

steps.description: Click the attribute's Edit anchor. Primary deterministic target: the recorded elementHash for the anchor (first <a> in the matched row). XPath provided as a robust fallback if the runtime resolves elements by XPath.
After clicking Edit, extract the edit page to verify we are on the attribute edit form.
steps.goal: Confirm attribute edit page loaded: capture page title, breadcrumb and presence of Attribute Code field to verify navigation succeeded.

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base admin URL including protocol and host (example: "http://dockerized-magento.local"). Tool will navigate to {base_url}/index.php/admin/catalog_product_attribute/.

input_schema.name: attribute_code
input_schema.description: Exact attribute code to find and open for edit (matches the 'Attribute Code' column). Example: "color".

input_schema.name: frontend_label
input_schema.description: Frontend label filter (visible label). Provide exact label text (e.g. "Color") or empty string to leave this filter blank.

input_schema.name: is_global
input_schema.description: Scope filter visible text or numeric value. Magento maps scope to integers: 0=Store View, 1=Website, 2=Global. Use the visible text (recommended) or the numeric value. Leave empty string to skip scope selection.

input_schema.name: wait_seconds_after_search
input_schema.description: Seconds to wait after clicking Search to allow grid refresh (default recommended: 1).
